requirement:
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. In a multipart label such as `impl[Thing/Trait]`, `/` separates
name parts. A slash within one part is encoded as `%2F`. Line numbers MUST NOT
form part of a selector.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` states only observable behavior, and the review roots and Implements edges are empty. Each clause describes the selector strings the system produces and resolves. I found no clause that prescribes a library, algorithm, signature, type, field or named interface.

- **Path form:** "`/`-separated path of segments from the file's root node", with the empty selector selecting the root. A different internal representation that still yields and resolves the same strings meets this.
- **Segment forms:** `kind[name]` for named nodes and `kind@hash` for anonymous nodes. The hash is "the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity hash". The identity hash is defined by `requirements.references.structural_hash`, which is cited for context only. The output is the same however it is computed.
- **Disambiguation:** `#N` with a one-based source-order position, and `line` nodes resolving on content. This is resolution and output behavior. Any lookup structure would satisfy it.
- **Percent-encoding:** the listed characters are encoded as UTF-8 bytes, and `/` separates name parts in multipart labels, with a slash inside a part encoded as `%2F`. An encoder written differently, such as a hand-rolled one or a library one, gives identical selectors.
- **No line numbers:** this is a restriction on the output.

Because every clause is a behavioral property, no implementation root needs a reference. Tests should cover the behavior.

behavioral: I found no test-adequacy gap. Each obligation in `requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` maps to a test with assertions that enforce it. I did not read implementation source.

- **`/`-separated path and empty selector selects root.**
  - `parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/selector.rs` checks that `parse_selector("")` is empty. It also parses multi-segment selectors and rejects malformed ones: `a//b`, `fn`, `fn[run`, `[run]` and `fn[run]x`.
  - `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` in `outline/tests.rs` asserts `outline.resolve("") == 0`. It also asserts that every nested selector resolves to a node whose stored selector equals it.
- **Named segment `kind[name]`.** `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` and `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` check many kinds, such as `mod[local]/fn[run]` and `struct[Thing]`. `parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments` checks `Segment::base` and the display form `fn[run]`.
- **Anonymous segment `kind@hash`, first 12 hex digits of the identity hash.**
  - `anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes` asserts a `use@` prefix and a length of 12 hex digits. It also asserts that selectors survive an insertion and that an edit to the node itself breaks resolution.
  - `anonymous_container_selectors_use_identity_hashes_and_survive_descendant_edits` asserts the selector equals `pair[items]/item@{identity_hash[..12]}`. It also asserts that identity and structural hashes differ and that the selector survives a descendant edit.
  - The parser tests reject `use@123`, a 13-digit hash and non-hex digits.
- **`#N` disambiguation, one-based and in source order.** `duplicate_names_are_numbered_in_source_order_without_line_numbers` asserts `fn[run]#1` and `fn[run]#2` map to the first and second declarations by byte offset. Swapping the declarations swaps the ordinals. `anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes` checks `#1`/`#2` on identical anonymous `use` nodes. The parser rejects `#0`, and an unnumbered ambiguous selector fails to resolve.
- **`line` exception.** `plain_text_lines_are_interchangeable_anonymous_nodes` asserts that identical lines get identical `line@…` selectors with no `#N`, and that the selector resolves. Whitespace-only differences leave the selector unchanged, while `twowords` differs.
- **Percent-encoding of `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`, `@` and whitespace as UTF-8 bytes, reversible.** `names_round_trip_through_percent_encoding` asserts the exact encoding of every listed character. It includes tab, NBSP and the ideographic space as multi-byte sequences. It asserts decode returns the original name and that raw `/`, a bad escape and raw whitespace are rejected. End-to-end cases are `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]` and `section[A%2FB]`.
- **Multipart labels.**
  - `parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments` checks that `impl[Thing/Trait%3CT%3E]` parses into two parts and that a slash inside a part encodes as `%2F`.
  - `selecting_multipart_impls_and_literal_slashes_preserves_label_boundaries` selects `impl[Thing/core::fmt::Display]`. It asserts that `impl[Thing%2Fcore::fmt::Display]` fails and that `section[A/B]` fails while `section[A%2FB]` succeeds.
- **No line numbers in selectors.** The duplicate-names test shifts the source by three lines. The selectors stay `fn[run]#1` and `fn[run]#2` while `line_start` changes.

The cited `requirements.references.structural_hash` is context only. The tests apply its identity hash to selectors, which is what the subject requires.

text: :::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. In a multipart label such as `impl[Thing/Trait]`, `/` separates
name parts. A slash within one part is encoded as `%2F`. Line numbers MUST NOT
form part of a selector.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
